reason: The text uses the ethnonym 'עִבְרִים' (Hebrews) to distinguish them as a distinct people separate from Egyptians. The phrase 'מִי שָׂמְךָ לְאִישׁ שַׂר וְשֹׁפֵט עָלֵינוּ' (Who made you a ruler and judge over us?) demonstrates collective consciousness and suggests the Hebrews conceive of themselves as a group ('us') capable of having leaders/judges. This indicates portrayal as a people with collective identity, transcending mere family ties or personal relationships, even if full political organization as a nation-state is not explicitly depicted.
